name: Finding the Minimum Value in a List
description: Write a program that finds the minimum value in a list.
code:
#Step 1: Define and initialize the list
values = [5, 8, 4, 78, 95, 12, 1, 0, 6, 35, 46]
#Step 2: Set the first value to be the minimum value so far.
min_value = values[0]
#Step 3: Iterate through the remaining values in the list and decide which one is the minimum value 
for i in range(1, len(values)): 
    # Step 3.1: Determine if the element at index i is the minimum value so far
    if (values[i] < min_value):
        min_value = values[i]
#Step 4: Print the minimum value in the list
print("Minimum value:", min_value)

commentList: We define the list referred by variable values to hold specified numbers. We initialize the list by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ].

3.content: #Step 2: Set the first value to be the minimum value so far.

commentList: We need variable min_value to store the minimum value of the list. We initialize this variable by the first value in the list because we initially assume that the first value is the minimum.

5.content: #Step 3: Iterate through the remaining values in the list and decide which one is the minimum value

commentList: We use a for loop to iterate over the remaining list indexes and searching for the minimum value. We need the remaining list indexes to start at 1 with every integer number up to but not including the list length. We get this sequence by calling the range(1,len(values)) function.

Note that the loop starts at 1 because we already checked the value at the index 0 of the list when initializing the variable min_value. Also note that the function len(values) returns the number of the values in the list.
Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

7.content: # Step 3.1: Determine if the element at index i is the minimum value so far

commentList: We need to compare the value at the index i of the list with the minimum value stored in variable min_value. If the value at index i is smaller than the minimum value, then we need to set the minimum value to the value of the element at index i.
If the list value at index i is less than the minimum value so far, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
This statement sets the minimum value to the value of the element at index i of the list.

10.content: #Step 4: Print the minimum value in the list

commentList:
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Minimum value:" and the value of variable min_value.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
